title: Root-knot nematodes in Irish potato - Kenya

Header: Root-knot nematodes in Irish potato - Kenya
Meloidogyne spp. Kigunyu Kia Waru in Kikuyu langauage

Prevention: Before planting, do soil testing at a nearby soil testing lab to check for any nematodes.
Do soil solarisation before planting, by using a black polythene bag spread over the entire soil for at least 4-6 weeks in hot sun to kill any present nematodes.
Irish potato with several seasons of a non-host crop, such as beans, maize, barley, wheat.
Clean farming equipment after use to prevent the spread of nematodes from one point to the other.
Plant nematode trap crops such as marigold (humus or
Essex varieties) to minimise damage to the main crop.
Monitoring: Start monitoring immediately after emergence, twice per month until harvesting.
Stunted, wilting and yellowish plants while there is plenty of water. 2.
Do a random uprooting of plants and check if the tubers have blister- like symptoms.
This can be done once per month. 3.
From uprooted plants, check for root knots or galls (swellings), which contain milky pinkish brown fluid inside. 4.
Nutritional deficiency shown on foliage such as chlorosis (infested plants are unable to take up water and nutrients from the soil).
It becomes too late to take action towards harvesting, or when the field soil is largely infested with the nematodes.
Direct Control: At the seedling stage, drench (flood) the crop and repeat the process when the plant reaches knee high (45cm).
Nimbecidine (azadirachtin) (usual dosage 50ml/20L) to drench as per the application advised.
Dig a small trench/ditch to restrict the movement of nematodes from the infested area to unaffected areas.
This ditch is dug between the affected area and the unaffected area.
Apply chitin from the crushed shells of crabs and shrimp into the soil to increase the predators of the nematode pest in the soil.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max. number of sprays, and restricted re-entry interval.
